pull_request.body:
closes #45 

Add cargo-deny configuration and CI workflow to the repository to enforce security and license compliance on every PR.

## Changes

### deny.toml (new)
- **Advisories:** Denies vulnerable, unmaintained, unsound, and yanked crates via the RustSec Advisory Database. This catches supply-chain risks before they reach production.
- **Licenses:** Denies copyleft licenses (GPL, AGPL, LGPL, MPL-2.0) and unlicensed crates. Allows the ecosystem-standard permissive licenses: MIT, Apache-2.0, Unicode-3.0, and ISC. Includes an explicit license exception for `clippy_utils` (pinned git dep from rust-clippy whose license file may not be detectable by cargo-deny from a git source).
- **Sources:** Blocks unknown registries and git repositories. Whitelists only `https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-clippy` for the pinned clippy_utils dependency. Any future git dep added without updating deny.toml will fail CI.
- **Bans:** Warns on duplicate crate versions to encourage dependency graph deduplication.

### .github/workflows/security.yml (new)
- Triggers on pushes and pull requests to `main` when dependency files change (`Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml`, `deny.toml`, or the workflow itself). Also supports manual `workflow_dispatch`.
- Runs `EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2` with `--all-features` to scan all workspace members.
- No separate Rust toolchain install needed — the action handles it internally.

## Why

As soroban-cost-linter brings in more external dependencies (Dylint, syn, clippy_utils via git), we need automated guardrails to ensure we aren’t accidentally inheriting vulnerable packages or copyleft-licensed code that violates ecosystem policies.

Closes #45
